proposed_global_claims.statement: A planar polynomial Keller map cannot have function-field degree three: degree three is generically three-sheeted, while Orevkov's 1987 primary theorem excludes constant Jacobian for a three-sheeted polynomial map C2 to C2.

For a finite locally free normal rank-three algebra over a characteristic-zero DVR, the geometric reduction of the trace-zero binary index cubic is GL2-equivalent to L1 L2 L3, L M^2, or L^3 according to ramification partition 1+1+1, 2+1, or 3.

After choosing a section primitive at every target boundary prime and a square-free product H of those primes, every theta+H T eta stays primitive at the boundary and has index D+H C T+H^2 B_2 T^2+H^3 A T^3; every remaining factor is a nonboundary scalar collision.

No nonconstant fixed divisor in C[P,Q] is invariant under both target translations, but the exact Keller differential congruence does not make a named fixed-section index ideal translation-stable; moving scalar collisions are not ramification.

The issue #3 no-unit countermodel reaches the finite-flat, normal, connected, rational, open-A2 stages, while adding boundary-only different support on the specified source open would produce an impossible degree-three Keller map.
